🇷🇸 Post-election "cleanup" in Serbia targets Kosovo and Mladić graffiti

Since the Student List won Sunday's election, activists and citizens across Serbia have been painting over graffiti and murals, and the targets are no longer just campaign slogans.

In central Belgrade on Thursday, activist Miodrag "Mio" Kapor and associates painted over the slogan "When the army returns to Kosovo" on Sremska Street. Kapor, an energy expert and independent activist, is not part of the Student List and in fact targeted its program too, saying he was removing the Kosovo claim in Serbia's constitution from the platforms of both the outgoing government and the students. He said he waited until after the vote because it was now safer. The move drew a wave of anger and threats online, with some demanding his arrest for "violating the Constitution." Kapor was attacked at a protest in Novi Sad in January after displaying Albanian and Croatian flags.

In Subotica, near the Hungarian border, citizens were filmed painting over a graffiti of General Ratko Mladić and the word "hero." Earlier this month, his mural in Niš was painted over after a student rally in the city and replaced with the slogan "Students Win." The mural read "He who the people remember has not died."

The wider cleanup began earlier in the week. Students in Blockade called on citizens to strip campaign posters and graffiti insulting the students, while citizens' assemblies and environmental group Eko straža repainted walls covered in slogans for Vučić's ruling party, including the Zeleni Venac underpass in Belgrade. The Youth Initiative for Human Rights, an NGO backed by Western donors including the US-based Mott Foundation, has long campaigned for the removal of what it calls hate graffiti and murals, with Mladić murals among its main targets.

🇷🇸 Serbian activists claim to have bags of shredded Finance Ministry documents

Belgrade Stays, an activist movement aligned with the student protests, says its "mobile teams" have obtained dozens of bags of finely shredded paper taken out of the Finance Ministry and the government's Directorate for Joint Services on Wednesday afternoon.

Video released by the group shows a van packed with the bags. Among the shreds are a few torn but readable pages, including the end of an official letter signed by a "Director, Prof. Dr. Dejan Đurđević" commenting on a draft law. The pile also includes a book with former president Aleksandar Vučić on the cover, notebooks, business cards and a conference badge.

The group says the material will be preserved as potential evidence and handed to the authorities after consulting the Student List, which won Sunday's election. "Nothing must be hidden, nothing must disappear without a trace," it wrote.

Belgrade Stays has not explained how it got the bags or from whom.

🟣 Binance hit by suspected multibillion-dollar hack

Billions of dollars in crypto drained out of hot wallets belonging to Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, on Thursday evening.

According to on-chain trackers, roughly $2.5 to $3.3 billion in ETH, stablecoins and more than 60 other tokens left two Binance hot wallets on Ethereum in under an hour, landing in a freshly created address that did not exist before Thursday. Some analysts put total outflows across all chains as high as $5.6 billion, though that figure is unverified. Etherscan has since tagged the receiving address as a "Binance Hot Wallet Exploiter," and the attacker's wallet was reportedly funded through the Tornado Cash mixer a day earlier.

Binance itself has not confirmed a breach, saying only that its security teams are investigating and that no impact on user funds has been confirmed.

Founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao was more direct, writing on X that it "looks like Binance was indeed hacked," while insisting user funds are safe. He said that as a shareholder he expects all losses to be fully covered.

Stablecoin issuers moved quickly. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT, and Circle froze around $823 million in USDC linked to the suspected attacker's wallets.

Bitcoin, Ether and BNB all dropped on the news.

If confirmed, it would be the largest crypto theft in history, dwarfing the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of 2025.
